title: How Pleasing, Lord! to See
description: How Pleasing, Lord! to See in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 928 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Family Affection from Religious Principles”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How pleas-ing, Lord! to see, How pure is the de-light, When mu-tual love, and love to thee, A fa-mi-ly u-nite!

lines: When mutual love, and love to thee,
As no increase of riches brings,
While mingled praise and mingled prayers
Where joy like morning dew distils,
And all the air is love.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
